content:
jay: FYI seeing a sustained p99 bump on /v1/generate (model: redwood-7B-quant) since the kernel-selection change this morning. p95 mostly stable but p99 up ~220ms :thinking:

maria: ugh. Is this across all routes or just that endpoint?

jay: looks concentrated on that route and a few similar long-context chat routes. throughput is unchanged, error rate low. Token-level waterfall shows a late tail around token 12-18.

devon: can you paste the token waterfall slice? also any KV hitrate diffs?

jay: pasted below from console probe:```route=/v1/generate p50=32ms p95=90ms p99=310ms tps=18 er=0.2%
token_latency_slice=[t0:5ms,t1-6:7ms,t7-11:12ms,t12-18:85ms,t19+:6ms]```

chris: interesting — that big spike at token 12-18 smells like a KV cache re-eval or a kernel fallback mid-request. Did the scheduler change batching heuristics too?

jay: we flipped kernel chooser to prefer fused-attn kernel for medium seqs (<=128). The affected traces have seq_len ~140 on first pass but dynamic trimming during decoding sometimes changes shapes. Might be misclassified at runtime.

maria: KV cache metrics show a 7% drop in hit_rate for that route after the change (from 92% -> 85%). Could explain the sudden recompute cost.

devon: if a request misses KV, we fall back to recomputing key/value which can trigger heavier kernels and more GEMM work. That maps to token waterfall tail.

sre-bot: alert created: INCIDENT-2026-176100 status=investigating owner=@devon link=https://incidents/reports/1761009876

chris: proposal for console KPI card updates: add a small inline KV hit-rate sparkline, token-waterfall micro-slices (0-5,6-11,12-23,24+), and kernel-variant attribution (percent requests served by kernel X/Y). That should make detective work faster.

maria: +1. Also recommend an annotation layer for config rollouts (so we can see kernel-chooser toggle time aligned with p99).

jay: can we pin json of a sample slow trace? snippet:```trace_id=abc123; kernels=[fused-attn->fallback-gemm]; kv_hit=false; decode_tokens=20; p99_token_index=14```

devon: good sample. For mitigation, can we force fallback-disabled or revert chooser? Or better: change chooser threshold from 128->160 for a short window.

chris: operationally safer to adjust threshold > flip entire feature. We can roll a canary: 10% traffic on route -> chooser=160 and compare per-route KPIs.

maria: i'll add a per-route comparison widget in the console: canary vs prod p50/p95/p99, kv_hit_rate, kernel_mix, throughput. Should be quick.

jay: thanks. Also can we add a derived metric: "p99_token_latency_contrib" where we attribute p99 regressions to token-slices so alerts can trigger on token-slice regressions rather than whole-route p99?

devon: yes — we already emit token_bucketed_latencies at 10-token granularity. We need a rollup job to compute contribution and then a console alert rule. I'll open a PR for the rollup tomorrow.

sre-bot: deploy-bot started: canary rollout for kernel-chooser-threshold -> 10% on /v1/generate by @chris
deploy-bot: canary finished: no 5xxs, small p95 delta (-3ms), p99 down in canary by 40ms vs prod.

jay: nice, looks promising. Next steps: 1) maria adds comparison widget and annotates the change time 2) devon implements p99_token_latency_contrib rollup + alert 3) chris waits 1h then increases canary to 50% or reverts based on data.

maria: working on the widget now, will tag the thread when done.

devon: opened PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/rollups/pull/412 — includes sample queries and alert rule draft.

jay: thanks team. if canary holds we'll keep new threshold. I'll capture the incident notes into postmortem template. :thumbsup:
